fact: Prime Minister Nchemba said on International Identity Day that national identity cards enable citizens to access banking, employment, SIM card registration and other government services.
The Prime Minister named banking, employment and SIM card registration as services the national ID enables access to.

The Prime Minister directed NIDA to deepen integration with institutions for employment, social services and economic activities, saying all institutions dealing with important services should join the system so data can be cross-checked.
TCRA's monitoring manager said biometric SIM registration identifies people registering lines and that national identification details linked to lines used in fraud can be blocked.
Ministry of Home Affairs figures say NIDA connected 17 institutions to its Registration and Identification System between July 2025 and April 2026, bringing the total connected to 147.
The 147 connected institutions comprise 66 public and 81 private institutions, per the Ministry of Home Affairs.
The Ministry of Home Affairs counted 147 institutions connected to NIDA's system, 66 public and 81 private, 17 added July 2025 to April 2026.

Biometric Update reports, citing a Daily News article, that Tanzania requires SIM registration with biometric identity verification using national ID cards to prevent fraud; no date is given for the requirement, so the published date is used.
system: SIM registration with biometric verification against national ID

fact: The NCFI Annual Financial Inclusion Report 2025, as reported, says the NIDA database is connected with 138 public and private institutions, improving e-KYC processes for banks, insurance companies and social security institutions.
The report names banks, insurance companies and social security institutions as using NIDA-connected e-KYC processes.
The report counts 138 public and private institutions connected to the NIDA database.
NIDA's director general said on 14 April 2025 that NIDA had connected its system with 128 institutions, 71 private and 57 public.
NIDA said it had received 56 institution applications from January to 12 April 2025 and expected 200 institutions connected to its systems by December 2025.
NIDA says consent-based eKYC against the national ID is in use for instant bank account opening and online company and TIN registration.
NIDA lists bank account opening and company and TIN registration (tax) among services using its eKYC.
NIDA counts 124 institutions integrated with its consent-based eKYC, 55 government and 69 private.
NIDA reports that the tax authority's taxpayer registration, bank KYC, health insurance and pension disbursement check people against the national ID.
NIDA names SIM registration (TCRA), health insurance (NHIF), social security, banks and tax (TRA) as sectors relying on the national ID.
NIDA reports 147+ institutions integrated and USD 66.4 million revenue generated from ID verification.
Government spokesman Gerson Msigwa said that by August 2026 institutions were linked to NIDA's registration and identification system and could verify the identity of the people they serve.

Msigwa said use of the national ID number has spread across sectors including taxpayer registration, financial services, health insurance, higher-education loans, TASAF social services and business registration.
Msigwa said 157 institutions, 72 government and 85 private, were linked to the NIDA system by August 2026.
NIDA says it has shared personal identification information through its Common Interface Gateway since 2018 with eligible stakeholders for eKYC and authentication alongside service provision.
